Subject: [PATCH] openvswitch: fix memory leak at failed datapath creation

ovs_dp_cmd_new()->ovs_dp_change()->ovs_dp_set_upcall_portids()
allocates array via kmalloc.
If for some reason new_vport() fails during ovs_dp_cmd_new()
dp->upcall_portids must be freed.
Add missing kfree.

Fixes: b83d23a2a38b ("openvswitch: Introduce per-cpu upcall dispatch")
Acked-by: Aaron Conole <aconole@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrey Zhadchenko <andrey.zhadchenko@virtuozzo.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220825020326.664073-1-andrey.zhadchenko@virtuozzo.com

diff --git a/net/openvswitch/datapath.c b/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
index 7e8a39a35627..6c9d153afbee 100644
--- a/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
+++ b/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
@@ -1802,7 +1802,7 @@ static int ovs_dp_cmd_new(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 				ovs_dp_reset_user_features(skb, info);
 		}
 
-		goto err_unlock_and_destroy_meters;
+		goto err_destroy_portids;
 	}
 
 	err = ovs_dp_cmd_fill_info(dp, reply, info->snd_portid,
@@ -1817,6 +1817,8 @@ static int ovs_dp_cmd_new(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	ovs_notify(&dp_datapath_genl_family, reply, info);
 	return 0;
 
+err_destroy_portids:
+	kfree(rcu_dereference_raw(dp->upcall_portids));
 err_unlock_and_destroy_meters:
 	ovs_unlock();
 	ovs_meters_exit(dp);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/openvswitch/datapath.c`**
- A new label `err_destroy_portids` was added to handle the cleanup of the `upcall_portids` array in case of an error during the `ovs_dp_cmd_new()` function.
- The line `kfree(rcu_dereference_raw(dp->upcall_portids));` was added under the new label to free the allocated memory for `upcall_portids` if the `new_vport()` function fails.

### Relationships
The modifications in `datapath.c` are directly related to fixing a memory leak that occurs when the `new_vport()` function fails during the execution of `ovs_dp_cmd_new()`. By adding the cleanup code to free the `upcall_portids`, the patch ensures that memory allocated via `kmalloc` is properly released, preventing potential memory leaks in the Open vSwitch implementation. This change is a direct response to the issue identified in the bug report, as indicated by the backtrace and the memory leak example provided in the patch description.
